content: 1. In biochemistry, a substrate refers to a specific molecule that undergoes a chemical reaction facilitated by an enzyme. 2. In biology, a substrate describes the natural environment or surface where an organism resides, grows, or attaches itself. 3. In chemistry, a substrate is the material that serves as a platform for chemical species to undergo catalytic reactions. 4. In electronics, a substrate can refer to a wafer, which is the foundational material used for the fabrication of semiconductor devices. 5. Additionally, in electronics, a substrate may denote the electrically insulating layer that forms part of the structure of a printed circuit board (PCB).
